 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Lionel Messi officially retired from international football in October and will not be playing for Argentina in their international friendly against Uruguay on Friday, November 13.
 The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner is not in Lionel Scaloni's 28-man squad for the international break in November, which will usher in a new era for the reigning world champions without their legendary captain.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Messi's absence is not due to an injury, fitness issue, or tactical choice, unlike in the past with international breaks. The Inter Miami superstar has brought his 21-year international career with Argentina to an end.
 Why Did Lionel Messi Retire From Argentina?
 On October 6, 2026, Messi played his final international match for Argentina in a friendly against Benin after announcing his retirement in August.
 The move marked the end of an extraordinary international career that lasted over 20 years and saw him become Argentina's top scorer.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Argentina's forward #10 Lionel Messi celebrates scoring his team's third goal during the international friendly football match between Argentina and Benin at the Mas Monumental stadium. (Photo by Luis ROBAYO / AFP via Getty Images)
 Messi has won four big international trophies with the national team: the 2022 FIFA World Cup, two Copa América titles and the 2022 Finalissima.
 Argentina will now have to face international tournaments without the player who guided them through their best modern era.
 Is Lionel Messi Injured or Dropped From Argentina's Squad?
 No. Messi has not been dropped or ruled out due to injury by Scaloni.
 Argentina revealed their first team of the post-Messi era on November 3, with 28 players to face Uruguay and Costa Rica in friendlies.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement There are also some familiar faces like Julian Alvarez, Alexis Mac Allister and Enzo Fernandez. But Messi is not included in the squad due to his retirement from international football.
 Other notable absences include Lautaro Martínez and Cristian Romero, who are out with injuries.
 When Is Argentina vs. Uruguay?
 Argentina will play Uruguay at La Bombonera in Buenos Aires on Friday, Nov. 13, at 8:00 p.m. local time (11:00 p.m. GMT).
 The friendly will be Argentina's first game without Messi after his retirement, and Scaloni will have a chance to start preparing for the next international cycle.
